Lord of the Rings. The books are full of so much useless filler. I also prefer the Hobbit films to the original book because it had a lot more lore, whereas the book had practically nothing. I'd go with the Shawshank Redemption if you want to count it (since technically it was originally a short story, not a whole book).

The movie does a good job of actually covering virtually everything in the story, but adding a lot of other stuff which makes it better overall.
Game of Thrones...after book 3, the series is a total chore to get through. HBO did it right and dumped a lot of fluff characters and actually keeps the story compelling.

Forrest Gump and the Shinning. Although the argument can be made in both cases that the movie wasn't the same story as the book. Forrest Gump the movie has almost nothing in common with the book. The Shinning book has a lot more of a supernatural twist on the plot instead of the father going crazy and some loose threads to the supernatural.

A lesser answer for me is the Count of Monte Cristo but that's because I hate reading French names.

Starship Troopers.

I know there are people who'll want to flay me alive for saying that. I'm sure the book was full of amazing new ideas and concepts back when it was written in 1959. But reading it 40+ years later, most of the ideas have been done to death in other books or media. (power suits, insectoid aliens etc) and it comes across as just another pulp sci-fi/war novel where our hero uses fancy techno-gadgets to blow up the evil aliens..

The movie on the other hand manages to combine, action, sci-fi, parody, an examination of nationalism, patriotism, propaganda and government control of the media, while leaning on the 4th wall so hard it damn near breaks. All while providing enough explosions and special effects to make Michael Bay blush.

Starship Troopers is just a beautiful movie.
